title: The World Wide Web
tagline: The invention that put the internet on the page.

events.title: The proposal
events.text: Tim Berners-Lee at CERN circulates “Information Management: A Proposal”, outlining a hypertext system — born of a need to share the web of his own scattered notes.

events.title: The first web server
events.text: Berners-Lee builds the first web browser/editor and server, connecting the world’s first website — info.cern.ch — to the internet.

events.title: The web goes public
events.text: The web becomes usable by anyone as Berners-Lee announces it on alt.hypertext and places it on the open internet.

events.title: The Web becomes visual
events.text: Mosaic, the graphical browser at NCSA, puts images inline and popularises the web for ordinary people.

events.title: The W3C is founded
events.text: Berners-Lee founds the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) at MIT to set web standards, instead of letting companies own the web.

events.title: Web 2.0: the web starts to talk back
events.text: The term “Web 2.0” takes off, marking the shift to user-generated content, social media and interactive pages.

events.title: The Web turned into the mobile web
events.text: Mobile overtakes desktop as the primary web access medium worldwide, reshaping design, speed and search.
